subject: Are you ready to elect a Democrat in Texas?

body:
here are the latest developments...
#
Peter,
There have been some major developments out of Texas recently, so today we wanted to get you up to speed on the latest.
Here’s what you need to know:
**FIRST – As soon as James Talarico became the official Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas, the GOP started pummeling him with attacks.** They know his message is already resonating with voters across the state, so they’re doing everything they can to tear him down.

subject: Thank You for Believing in Our Campaign!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Canepa for Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder 2026 committee, ID #1486383**
body:

| | |
---
| Friends,

As the votes continue to be counted, I am humbled and grateful by the support our campaign has received throughout San Mateo County.

While this campaign carried my name, this victory belongs to all of us.

I want to sincerely thank every person who played a role in this journey. Thank you to the voters who placed their trust in me. Thank you to our donors whose generosity helped us share our message. Thank you to our volunteers who walked precincts, made phone calls, sent text messages, hosted events, and spent countless hours helping our campaign reach voters across the county. Thank you to my family and friends whose encouragement and support sustained me through every step of this race.

This campaign was built around a commitment to protecting our elections, ensuring fair and accurate property assessments, modernizing public records, and providing outstanding service to the people of San Mateo County. Together, we shared a vision of an Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder-Chief Election Officer's Office that is accessible, transparent, efficient, and worthy of the public's trust.

The campaign trail brought me into neighborhoods and communities throughout the county, where I had the opportunity to listen to residents, hear their concerns, and learn from their experiences. Those conversations reinforced why public service matters and why local government can make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

I am especially grateful for the confidence you have placed in me. Serving the people of San Mateo County is a responsibility I do not take lightly. I am committed to working every day to earn your trust and to build an office that residents can be proud of.

Thank you for believing in this campaign, for believing in public service, and for believing in the future of San Mateo County.

I look forward to serving you and getting to work.

With gratitude,
David Canepa
Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder-Chief Election Officer Elect
San Mateo County

name: Chris Pappas
subject: I’d be the first gay man in the U.S. Senate
body:
My community showed me what’s possible.
| When I was a kid, reading this kind of headline would have been unimaginable, friend: [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/111167?t=6&akid=24871%2E878179%2ENveGNo) Growing up as a gay person in New Hampshire, I never imagined I could live out — let alone run for U.S. Senate. **But my community showed me what's possible.** You helped me win _four times_ in one of the most competitive congressional districts in the country.

We’ve made tremendous progress since I was younger. But there’s still something we’ve never done. **We’ve never elected a gay man to the Senate.**

To be clear I’m not running for Senate just to make history. I’m in this race for the people of New Hampshire –** _all of us_**. But the prospect of moving the needle of progress forward is deeply meaningful to me.

This is an opportunity for representation in the Senate. It’s also important that LGBTQ+ people have more seats at the table at a time when our rights are coming under attack.

**We can win this election for the people of New Hampshire, charting a path forward for our shared future – and we can tear down barriers and make history at the same time.**

[Will you split a $10 contribution between my campaign and Voter Protection Project right now to stand with me in this historic fight?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/111167?t=7&akid=24871%2E878179%2ENveGNo)

**Thank you for supporting me in this campaign, friend.** No matter who you are, who you love, who you pray to, or where you're from — know that I'll always have your back.

With gratitude,

Chris

But there’s still something we’ve never done. We’ve never elected a gay man to the Senate. To be clear I’m not running for Senate just to make history. I’m in this race for the people of New Hampshire – all of us. But the prospect of moving the needle of progress forward is deeply meaningful to me. This is an opportunity for representation in the Senate. It’s also important that LGBTQ+ people have more seats at the table at a time when our rights are coming under attack. We can win this election for the people of New Hampshire, charting a path forward for our shared future – and we can tear down barriers and make history at the same time. Thank you for supporting me in this campaign, friend. No matter who you are, who you love, who you pray to, or where you're from — know that I'll always have your back. With gratitude, Chris 878179 | | Paid for by VPP (www.protectvoting.org) Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. 401 2nd Ave. S, Ste. 303, Seattle, WA 98104 The Voter Protection Project is on an important mission: To end partisan gerrymandering and voter suppression by electing candidates at the state and federal levels that are forceful advocates for voting rights. ## US Strikes Iran after Intercepting Drones
U.S. forces [struck Iranian coastal radar sites](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU8DmZGxje0JHGxCNptuiGqgDN4xpuUqGvXtV3SwF5ikglfS0___z-f0CSmnsv6GHQPHYyp4UUZmrNNJxDV9I6UK5QLaUln5KJQnJZUV0grppgVSfk2mXUJEVKhbDL3z0ivrP4Z2C9H4Hu3QKwA96Bm8sdrB7Kx2Hx6cbVO4bdJK10vpe9OpLxeVNqCGQXmjoTESl8RH7f4eqfCGMb-OJ9ZuPvY2h435QY3-1aixUeN1Xd1cvub72ajxVjdqlP_PSQKYYf4mcbdKUAQlRhIQGeubiQxnmTcksdSjIIl0I0ZisZ45ipihojgf3cZ7bmtYHlfKOZF1jZHrDim_k_GP5nwG9S8AAP__5AiJvw) on Saturday after shooting down drones launched by Iran toward regional traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command said the U.S. struck Iran's surveillance sites in Goruk and Qeshm Island, which are both on the Strait of Hormuz. Iran also fired seven ballistic missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said it [targeted U.S. bases there](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8GMiPb_E7g4JLJ9tILUYOboW8be-XuWTT39CfmFTatTyrVV38-5g8gpvT4DQcG3fKc8BRGVSzzU0QLfaJQgXSC7JQempPw7K0fjB2MHecIxK-5q2PYED22NQY3Tnbyw3Tr6z104-QQVxv7JQ7DbYKba6NbonWub_0CNYWrzQ52dNZOrmv8Mm6-7cD3vZ-6FqrOYiTNpfmbKemOG7_yN5ZmzUfNYVf9kqr9Vfl75e_neTa6yGXRJNQryYXjQv8qfz8oRkaDIBd4igFVWD_FXIIEyawZRIGNkKIY2BTLmxmGZ1p3FBNLTiiGQVHUbAwF6xLi10nMJMNYdfZxAPF7nP7o0e_g_wcAAP__RZSOcg) in retaliation for U.S. strikes and fired on four tankers attempting to cross the strait without its permission. Centcom said: _" Initial assessments indicate [six of the missiles launched by Iran were intercepted](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwRsRvv7CA0MXb-na0boxl3BbDBGQWH77Kn2Fzkf6Sef_dV2vyIHj_RN3MtWlNdJRAtVKeX2WUjP_UOGM8cDiOd5riiWsoGCUapRqWi1yONe-scYRAXUNmXbSSsOo56HxRmsARHebLW1uBBo20POoYNIzdji3DZu3pkY1tUrptr_AbXLQ9QjDALrvUPSKLNeUL9-JY_XkwplelC9b2ptgfK2PIroPAYuApXryHMJ7E7A8UuDtFLBYchQLCViGuQXdz_JZ5M6BK-ZTFp9SLdKmI8r3V8YobU6RioClycY-Dg6ByziJXt135D-_qf8K9jLwGwAA__-bZIAM) and a seventh did not reach its intended target. There are currently no reports of harm to U.S. personnel, and Iranian claims of damaging U.S. 5th fleet headquarters in Bahrain are false."_

Pulte, who currently serves as the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, would be limited to serving 210 days in an acting capacity. Trump said: _"I 'd like to see it smaller. I think there are a lot of people in there that shouldn't be there."_ The Office of the Director of National Intelligence [oversees 18 U.S. intelligence agencies](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu4yAQheGnwZ2j8WBjp6DYxl223dIiYQizi8GCSaLs01_lvsKtj_RJ5_9z2S6OE-f7b7eTlVC2TK-WSITq9mhNKv-jxtXll2uR811KbmlDQNOD6WHevOP03sbO20CEpDuyw7zAgmY5T120C531cDUDXj3CiBq9RtAzhAUm443r2H40MDAPAMswnvA6B9Sjw2nCZdROjUCepdTT38JZIoX0Lk-qp1vZu2SjyNGU_qVwVbhKpMgpfTaFayw7fQ4pXJ3fOXOT6oRLVrhO5wERdS_1sR_98UhCvc_clxD4Rn3j_6Rw7ar1x4tT4mZmNcJ9d_ytd_KjXE-LXwEAAP__zsh-fg), but it's unclear what power Pulte would have to carry out firings at other agencies, such as the CIA.

**Whatever happened to Mark Spitz?** Mark Spitz is one of the greatest athletes of the 20th century, a swimmer who peaked so spectacularly that his story has two distinct halves: his improbable triumph in the 1972 Munich Olympics, and then the long, sometimes awkward process of being a living legend. He was in the water before he could really walk, and by age 10 he held 17 national age-group records. The destination always seemed obvious. But getting there wasn't. Spitz arrived at the 1968 Mexico City Games loudly predicting six gold medals and left with two relay golds and a bruised ego. The humiliation turned out to be the best thing that ever happened to him. Four years later in Munich, he entered seven events over eight days and won every single one, setting a world record each time. [You can see highlights here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwjAQxvGncTaiyzk4YfCAhJA60LWj5SRnctTEKD5i0aev6Ct0_T7pN_y_Lu7iOfJy_fR3shKSW6jkSCK0umfOsvI3ZV79UnyeeblKWnJ0CGh2YHbQuclzfLm2mmwgQtIV2abroUfTH_bVbJtx9GHqsQPS3sOgBw1NGBHHyRxMgIrtWwMDXQPQN22NQxdQtx73e-xb7VULNLGktb4lXmSmEF9po7Ue072KdhZ5ZKWPCs8Kz6WU-pWe8hzo_b8XL-Os9HlT-vQhx9vPaTvcHFSrnR6FY-RsOtXC9e45_pHyrw6bxd8AAAD__8BwceE). Afterwards, the [photograph of him in his swimsuit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGSpCAUgOHTYKaFT0E6INjErDfd0KLloW8bwYI3bfWcfmrmCnOB_6_6_t2Xu6NIafvrDrQc8pLwqhGZsSwftXKhJ1YqLl2u7pQ2zqnGBSToVupWTot3FN_L2HgbEAGHBm0_GWlAm5tqduuU96ofDJhw65Wb-qBXrxAfPoSbnkJD9rsmtZx6KU0_dvCYAgyjA6XAjIMTo0RPnEv3P1PiHUN85xeWbs1HE-3OfFYx_BEwC5hpzYlWOtyGtUvIAuZzz5wFzJyr1Ko9XHm29ST-bC_ivT3Qu1gFzE2x_rwoRqp6EqPcDkfxZ8K_knlZ-AoAAP__UT547w), seven medals draped around his neck, became the best-selling sports poster of the decade. America couldn't get enough of swimmer Mark Spitz. Then came the awkward part. He was 22, absurdly famous, and everyone wanted a piece of him: razor commercials, milk campaigns, [TV variety shows](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFy6yAQgOHToM6a1YIEKiheo84vZUoNMotFjIQH1lZ8-4xzhdT_zFf8n-f57GKK-_W_28hyyPNOR03ETGV-1Mol3qjG4vbD1TXuV857TTMCDicYTqBn72J6zarxNhAhyYZspw0YHMzYN6s16jL6xSjQQQevR2mGzi1S9f7iO4CxifatwQC6AzCdanHRAaVy2PdolHRCAfnIubRfOe68Ukiv_KTSXvLWJLsy36uQ_wROAqfjONpXfvBjoXcXONU1F64CJ6lUgNv27T9MU6y_HzGlWActFFw3F9Ovx3-a8LT4EwAA___1C3Bf), a Hollywood career that critics politely destroyed. He made $7 million in two years and later admitted he hadn't been remotely prepared for any of it. He retreated into real estate in Beverly Hills, did some Olympic commentary for ABC, and tried one last comeback at 41, falling two seconds short of qualifying for Barcelona in 1992. It was an easy effort to mock, but in fact, Spitz had cracked the world top 30 in his sport at middle age. Mark Spitz is one of the greatest athletes of the 20th century, a swimmer who peaked so spectacularly that his story has two distinct halves: his improbable triumph in the 1972 Munich Olympics, and then the long, sometimes awkward process of being a living legend. He was in the water before he could really walk, and by age 10 he held 17 national age-group records. The destination always seemed obvious. But getting there wasn't. Spitz arrived at the 1968 Mexico City Games loudly predicting six gold medals and left with two relay golds and a bruised ego. The humiliation turned out to be the best thing that ever happened to him. Four years later in Munich, he entered seven events over eight days and won every single one, setting a world record each time. . Afterwards, the , seven medals draped around his neck, became the best-selling sports poster of the decade. America couldn't get enough of swimmer Mark Spitz. Then came the awkward part. He was 22, absurdly famous, and everyone wanted a piece of him: razor commercials, milk campaigns, , a Hollywood career that critics politely destroyed. He made $7 million in two years and later admitted he hadn't been remotely prepared for any of it. He retreated into real estate in Beverly Hills, did some Olympic commentary for ABC, and tried one last comeback at 41, falling two seconds short of qualifying for Barcelona in 1992. It was an easy effort to mock, but in fact, Spitz had cracked the world top 30 in his sport at middle age. Today, in Los Angeles with his wife, Suzy; his two sons live nearby. He gives motivational speeches, stays connected to the swimming world, and holds a place in history that even Olympic legend Michael Phelps could only partially dislodge.
